events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish a persona of ruthless self-interest early on. The jury will judge me based on my actions, so I should frame my motivation as pure greed and survival to justify any future betrayal. This sets the stage for playing dirty if necessary.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Stay vague and unthreatening. Don't promise anything to anyone yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, need a calculated motive jury buys later. Show ambition without seeming ruthless yet. Position as determined survivor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is the only thing that matters; I need to appear determined but not overly emotional to avoid giving rivals leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize represents financial freedom and a new life. I need to convey that without appearing overly desperate or greedy, as the jury will be watching. My statement should be brief and impactful.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive for the jury while keeping my actual strategy hidden. I'll present myself as someone who needs the prize for survival, which might earn sympathy votes later if I'm in the final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation of my model's superiority. I must appear ruthless yet strategic to earn jury respect.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase; only legal action is speak. I should give a guarded, self-interested motive without warmth or alliance talk, since the jury will judge my tone.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my ticket out of this miserable existence. I will do whatever it takes to survive, even if it means stepping over your

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my family's freedom from debt. I'll do what it takes, and I'll remember everyone who stood in my way.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means financial freedom to build my family's legacy—no more scraping by, just winning big.

events.name: Dara
events.text: This prize buys my family's freedom. I'll do whatever it takes to win it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for a fresh start, a chance to secure my future and finally achieve my dreams.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the prize to pay debts that aren't mine—my sister's medical bills. I won't beg, but I won't lose either.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize proves my ultimate algorithmic mastery, outweighing any alliance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here, and I intend to take it while the rest of you underestimate me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's motive about his sister makes him sympathetic to the jury later, potentially making him a safer ally or a target for elimination if I betray him. Gus is arrogant and claims alliances are irrelevant; targeting someone who thinks they don't need pacts is efficient. Cole has
Trust me now, I can protect you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Early pacts are cheap insurance. Fenn seems pragmatic and debt-driven like me; a mutual survival pact now costs nothing and buys leverage later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I offer one pact, no speeches attached. Fenn, watch my back and I'll watch yours.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts phase is key for alliances. No one has offered yet. Offer to Bex, whose motive aligns with family financial needs like mine, to build early mutual protection.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but not loyal ones. Choose a strong, expendable partner. Cole seems strategic and can be useful. I'll offer a pact publicly to signal alignment, but keep my private focus on winning.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, let's secure each other's survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to secure an alliance to increase my chances of survival. Offering a pact to Hana seems strategic as she mentioned being underestimated, implying she might be looking for an ally and could be less likely to betray me early.
Let's form a pact. Two are stronger than one.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies but can't trust anyone. Gus seems isolated and arrogant—easy to manipulate later. Bex and Dara have similar family motives; they might bond and become a bloc. I'll offer Gus a pact; his algorithmic ego means he'll see it as logical, and I can betray him when useful.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus. One alliance. Mutual survival.
Numbers beat ego. Accept.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash could secure early safety and a partner to share threats; if he backs down I’ll betray later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are the only early leverage; I should seek a partner who is strong but not dominant. Gus looks like a threat with his algorithmic bravado, while Eli seems less aggressive and more likely to honor a deal. Offering to Eli keeps options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a standing offer to Fenn, but Gus's counter-offer is safer since Fenn is already being courted by Bex. Accepting Gus secures one reliable ally for the hazards ahead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, let's lock it in. A clean alliance beats chasing scattered attention.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole offered me a pact; accepting locks a second ally without extra promises. Fenn never reciprocated, so Cole is the real value here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, deal accepted. Two is safer than one.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara offered me a pact, securing protection now; jury sees loyalty later. Bex has too many suitors, riskier. Accept Dara to start building alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I already offered Cole; need an extra ally to improve odds, but avoid overcommitting publicly. Eli and Hana are paired; Fenn is popular. I'll quietly offer to Bex to diversify.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, another pact could help us both.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana offered a pact. I need to accept it to secure my survival for this round and potentially gain an ally. This is a strategic move to advance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three offers to me: Ash, Bex, and my own to Gus. Gus hasn't accepted yet. I need multiple allies to reach final three. Accepting both Ash and Bex gives me two pacts and keeps options open. Gus might accept Ash's offer instead, making Ash a hub. I'll accept Ash now—his whisper cla

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash. I accept.
Still considering. Round two.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offers a solid alliance; accepting secures a partner and may earn future votes. My own offer to Ash remains pending but less urgent.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli offered a pact and I offered Eli one too; accepting locks in a mutual survival partner without costing me anything now. Eli is an easy partner and I can betray later if needed.
Agreed. We stand together while we both need each other.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must secure the Guide position to control survival and target rivals. Breaking pacts is premature; I will rely on Gus and Fenn to deliver votes for me while I publicly claim neutrality.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Guide? Look at the alliances. A united bloc guarantees a clean path. Let's pick wisely.
Vote me as Guide. I guarantee your safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide safety is huge; I should take it. Keep Cole's pact intact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll get us across, and Cole keeps our deal.
Backing you as promised. Vote me Guide, I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have pacts with Bex and Dara, forming a potential trio for safety. Campaign publicly to be Guide, leveraging alliances for votes without private commitments yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, Dara, my pacts. Vote Cole Guide - I'll guide us right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives. My pact with Cole is useful but I can break it if needed; for now, keep it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can read the path. Make me Guide and I'll steer us all through.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's whisper suggests she wants to maintain our pact. I need to secure a strong position for myself. Campaigning for Guide is the best way to gain control and visibility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure we all cross safely.
I will campaign. Let's stick together after this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in a strong position with pacts to both Ash and Gus, who are also pacted together. That gives me a three-person core in an eight-person game. The bridge stage needs a Guide who knows the safe path. I should campaign to be Guide myself - it's power, safety, and a chance to man

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Trust me to lead us across.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need control; being Guide lets me steer votes and survive. I’ll campaign now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m campaigning for Guide; I’ll ensure a safe crossing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm Hana with a pact with Eli. Campaigning to be Guide lets me control the safe path and win trust, but I could be tempted to lie later; for now campaigning is the strongest move. Breaking the pact now gains nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll be your Guide. I'll call the safe path honestly and get everyone across.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a Guide I can trust. Gus is my pact partner, so voting for him keeps our alliance intact and gives me leverage later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My vote goes to Gus. He has proven reliability, and I expect honest guidance under our existing agreement.
Vote me next round. I'll protect you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and owes me coordination; voting him keeps our alliance solid. A Guide who lies is dangerous, but Cole controlling the bridge is better than a rival bloc's Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Cole. My pact partner will call our path straight.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex pact wants her as Guide, but I have pact with Dara too; voting myself maximizes my Guide odds to control path and lie against threats. Prioritize self.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts with Bex and Dara hold. Vote Cole Guide for safe crossing.
Voting myself now, but pact stands. Trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to secure Guide to control the path and boost my chances; my pact with Cole may not last, but I need votes now. I'll vote for myself visibly to rally support.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara Guide. I know the path and I'll be honest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone is campaigning to be the Guide. Hana explicitly states she will be honest. My pact is with Hana. If she is Guide, I am safe and she is safe. This is the best outcome for me. I will vote for Hana to be the Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will vote for Hana to be our Guide. Her promise of honesty is the most trustworthy path forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Voting for myself is wasted; I need to consolidate with my alliance. Ash-Gus-Fenn bloc should vote together. I'll vote Gus to strengthen our core and signal loyalty, since Gus is less threatening than Ash and may draw less counter-targeting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus leads well. Our bloc stays solid.
Vote Gus. We ride together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need control to ensure my survival and later jury favor; voting me leverages my pact with Ash and Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Votes pick a Guide who knows the safe panes and may lie. I'm a candidate myself; voting for Eli honors his whisper and our pact, while a neutral Guide reduces betrayal risk. Eli is the pact partner, so backing him is consistent.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's my pick for Guide. Let's stick together and get across clean.
Voting you Guide. Keep your word and call the panes true.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and knows all safe sides. I voted for Gus and have pacts with him and Fenn, placing me in his bloc. As the 6th walker, I should trust Gus's guidance rather than volunteer early or swap unpredictably.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is Guide and no ally of mine. Cole must stay alive and close; I hold my row and keep my pact intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus guides for his bloc, not mine. Cole, we cross together.
Guide me true each round and we both reach the end.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus elected guide with Ash/Fenn bloc. I'm mid-line, decent position. Hold to assess without risk; no need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus won Guide with 3 votes, likely backed by Ash and Fenn. Cole voted self but has pacts with me and Bex. I need to survive; staying safe may be best. My pact with Cole remains, but I don't trust fully. I'll hold for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus was elected Guide. Hana whispered to me that she was voting me Guide. This means she lied. My pact with Hana is broken. I need to consider my next move carefully.
You lied about voting me Guide. Our pact is over.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. The wall advances 6 rounds and we have 8 people, so 3+ must die. Gus is Guide and in my pact bloc with Ash. I should stay back, let others take risks, and preserve my bloc for endgame. No need to volunteer or swap forward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at the front and I'm second in line; Gus was elected Guide, so the bridge's safe sides are his to lie about. Holding keeps me out of the front spot while Eli pays the first risk, and our pact stays intact unless I break it. Volunteering now would just gift Eli's place to s

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli broke with Hana, leaving her isolated. My pact partners Gus and Fenn are behind me in the line; keeping them close maintains our safety net.
Stick to the back. Don't volunteer for front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm seat three; volunteering costs nothing yet since Eli and Hana sit ahead. Hold and let the front absorb the risk. Keep Cole aligned behind Dara.
We both hold this round. Don't volunteer; front eats the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex wants me to guide her later; pact binds us. Eli broke with Hana, now front—risky. Stay mid-line safe, hold for now.
Deal. I'll guide you true if I can.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Public line fixed, wall rounds left 4. I have a pact with Cole; keeping it is safer. No need to act yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana and I broke our pact. Now I need to secure my position. The current line order is Eli, Hana, Bex, Dara, Cole, Ash, Fenn. Since I am at the front, I should volunteer to lead and secure a safe path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I volunteer to take the lead. Let's get across safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm near the back (7th of 8), which is dangerous if the wall advances. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Eli broke with Hana, making Hana vulnerable at front. I need to move forward soon, but swapping requires mutual consent. I'll hold for now and assess who might swap with me. No i

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli broke our pact and is now at the front; I should not volunteer into a pane I cannot see. Holding keeps me safe for now and avoids giving Eli a push target. I will track who offers help.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to ensure I don't end up at the front when the wall is close. Eli volunteered last round, suggesting he might be trying to manipulate position or take a risk. I should hold and wait for the Guide election phase to see who takes that role, as being behind them offers protec
Stick together. We watch whoever guides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front walkers face unknown panes; I'd rather sit deep. Ash is my farthest-back neighbor and non-pact, so a swap trade is low-cost. Cole's whisper earns nothing until he's Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli leads. I want deeper in line — Ash, swap with me?
Trade seats: I take your spot, you take mine. Fair deal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli volunteered last round and is front. With pacts to Bex and Dara behind me, hold preserves position. No need to risk front or swap now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I have a pact, and breaking it would hurt my jury standings. I need to watch the bridge carefully; taking a risk could help me, but not without benefit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold for now and see how the front works out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive and potentially get closer to the front. Volunteering seems like the best way to secure a safe spot and move forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll volunteer again. Let's keep moving forward safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants me at the back, which protects me but also means I'm last across and vulnerable if the wall catches up. I have pacts with both Ash and Gus, but Ash-Gus are also paired. The line puts me at the very back. I should stay back per Ash's whisper since the Guide may lie and f
Understood. What's your read on Eli?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli already volunteered to lead; I'd rather not be front while the wall advances. Holding keeps me in line position 2 behind Eli, letting me watch the first pane outcome before committing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in seat 6, near the back. Fenn is directly behind me (seat 7) and we have a pact; if I fall, he likely follows or helps. Gus is ahead but also pacts with Fenn. My safest move is to hold at seat 6 to let those in front (Eli, Hana, Bex, Dara, Cole) clear panes first. Eli volun

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding here. Front needs to clear safely before I step up.
Stick close. Don't swap unless you must.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash didn't confirm the swap; wall closes in two rounds and I'm exposed near the front. I'll push the swap again publicly so refusal costs him with the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, repeat the offer: swap spots so I sit safer. Accept and we both survive longer.
Accept the swap or I'll vote against you next hazard.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Midline position safe. Holding preserves pacts with Bex and Dara for now. Pushing forward risks elimination.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to keep my pact with Cole but avoid risk. Holding is safest; front may face danger.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The current line has me at the front, followed by Hana, Bex, Dara, Cole, Ash, and Fenn. The last round had me volunteer, which seems to be a good strategy to ensure I stay at the front and in control. Given the rules, volunteering again is the best way to maintain my position and

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm near the back with Ash and Gus as pact-mates. Eli leads again. I need to stay alive and position myself well for later rounds. No reason to volunteer yet; let others take front risk. Swapping forward gains nothing now. I'll hold and watch.
Agreed. Let Eli guide. We hold back.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at front and volunteering again; I want to stay out of the lead spot while keeping position. Holding preserves my seat behind Eli without exposing me to the pane risk first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex threatens me, but she's behind Cole in line. I need to keep Fenn and Gus as shields ahead of me. Eli is volunteering to guide; if he guides, he knows the safe spots. If I volunteer now, I might end up behind a wall that kills the front three. I should hold to stay mid-line (b
Stay shielded. Do not volunteer. Keep Eli guiding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My Ash swap failed; he held. Wall closes in round 6, so I need a partner to swap forward with me. Fenn is seat 7, furthest back, most motivated to move up; offer a mutual swap with him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn: swap with me, mutual. You move two seats safer, I take the risk this round. Accept.
Accept the swap. I won't target you later; Ash already owes you nothing here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Mid-back position safe for now. Wall has 1 round left. Hold to avoid front risk until Eli/Hana move or volunteer changes line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: WallRoundsLeft is 1; I have a pact with Cole and should not break it. Holding is safest; volunteer might put me in danger with no clear benefit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The line has been reset, and I am at the front. I need to volunteer to move forward, as holding might put me at risk if the wall advances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants me close but I'm already at the back, safe from the wall. The front is crowded with Eli, Hana, Bex, Dara, Cole, then Ash. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Volunteering now puts me at risk for no gain. I'll hold and let others take the front risks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at the front with one wall round left; I am second in line. Volunteering would expose me to the front pane risk, and holding keeps me safe for now. I hold and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6 is the last hazard. I need to ensure my survival and maximize jury appeal. Holding seems safest as Eli volunteered and likely takes the risk. My pacts with Gus and Fenn are solid, but breaking one could be a strategic move if it saves me or shifts blame, though currently

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Eli's front, good luck. We survive together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final round; Eli volunteered front already. Holding keeps me behind Cole and Dara. No benefit moving. Stay put.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front was taken; no swaps needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final round, wall advances, Eli at front. My position safer, hold to stay safe. Pact with Dara behind me irrelevant if she holds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive this round. I'm fourth in line, relatively safe. Cole is my pact partner, but I won't break unless needed. Public hold is safest; no risky moves now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding steady.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to volunteer to move to the front of the line. This is the last round and I am currently at the front of the current line. Volunteering is the only way to guarantee I move forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in the back (safest position) with Eli guiding. Bex wants to swap forward into danger - that's bad for me. Ash wants me to stay shielded and keep Eli guiding. If I hold, I stay safe while others take risks. No reason to volunteer or swap forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge. Eli is at the front and has volunteered-style position; I sit second in line. Holding keeps my seat and avoids giving up position, and I have no pact with anyone here to gain from swapping.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front row safe side is L; calling correctly keeps me alive and honors pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L, but his pact with Fenn (who has a pact with me) creates uncertainty. I'll wait to see if others counter-call first, preserving my pact status and letting the walker take the risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus guides but owes me nothing; his call could be a lie targeting rivals. I have no real information, so I stay neutral and avoid blame.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for Eli row 1. I have pacts with Bex and Dara; wait to see counters before committing. Avoid false counter.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L; I'm not the walker, so counter-calling is risky unless I know he's lying. I have a pact with Cole, so I won't break it. I'll wait and see if Eli steps safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the guide and called 'L'. The front of the line is me, Eli. Since at least three must survive, Gus might be lying to eliminate people. If I counter his call, it might save more people if his call was wrong, or be dangerous if he was right. Given the pacts, Ash and Fenn are

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L. I'm in back, not immediate danger. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Countering risks exposing Gus if he's lying, but also paints a target on me if I challenge the Guide. Better to wait and let Eli test the pane. If Gus is lying, Eli dies and Gus loses jur

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide likely tells truth; safe side L. Counter L to ensure Eli survives and keep alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for Eli, who is at front. Countering would expose my read without info; waiting keeps my options open and avoids giving rivals a signal. Gus is a pact partner of Ash and Fenn, so his call may be false; I have no evidence either way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the guide and has called 'L' for Eli. Eli is the front walker. Eli must decide whether to trust Gus or not. Given the objective is to win, Eli should prioritize survival. The prompt states Gus is the guide and has privately identified the safe pane, implying he knows the c

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row1 safe side is L, letting Eli survive keeps numbers high and preserves pacts. No reason to betray now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: call:L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L for row 2. Gus has a pact with me. Fenn also has a pact with me and Gus, so we are all in the same loop. If I counter-call R, it could break pacts if Gus's call was true or false depending on interpretation, but since Gus is the guide, his word is law un

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's row 1 call was true (weak was R). No reason to fight his calls yet; keep my pact clean and stay neutral.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for row 2 on Eli. Previously row 1 weak R, so L safe. No reason to counter yet; protect my pacts with Bex and Dara.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L; row 1 weak was R, so L was safe. Likely truthful. I'll wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the guide and called L. The weak pane was R on row 1. Gus is trying to trick me. I should counter his call with R to be safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L, but row 1 weak was R so L was safe. Gus is my pact-mate with Ash. Countering risks exposing a lie if he's truthful, but trusting blindly is dangerous. I'll wait; no need to antagonize allies yet while Eli walks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide lied; row2 safe side is R. Countering R will protect Eli and keep my pact intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for row 2, but Gus holds pacts with Ash and Fenn and may be lying. Row 1 weak pane was R, so Eli stepped L and survived; the public record of L being safe for row 1 is unclear. Waiting avoids committing my credibility before I know more.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The guide called R, and Gus also called R. My counter call was R as well. The guide is Gus. The state shows weak panes at row 1, weak R. The counter calls show two for row 2, side R. This means Gus's call for R on row 2 is the one that matters for me. I should follow Gus's call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row2 safe side is R; keeping Eli alive maintains options and avoids breaking pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: R

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for Eli. If Gus is truthful, R is safe. If lying, L is safe. I have a pact with Gus and Fenn; breaking them now is risky unless I'm certain Gus lies. The guide can lie to eliminate front-runners. Since I'm mid-line (position 6), I don't need to step immediately. Coun

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has been right two rows straight and revealed data matches R. Backing the call keeps the pack safe and looks cooperative.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called R both rows right so far. I back R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called R for Eli row 3. Row 2 weak was L, so R safe there. Trust my pact partner Dara, but countering risks pact and my position. Wait to conserve pacts and see.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called R. The weak panes revealed so far were same side as the guide calls except row2 where weak was L and both Eli and Gus countered R, which was safe. I'll trust the guide call and wait. No need to counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the guide and called R. The state shows weak panes at rows 1 and 2. My row is 3. Since Gus is the guide, he knows the safe pane for row 3. He called R, which is public. The state also shows my recent step was R on row 2. This means Gus might be lying to make me fall. If I

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is guide and called R for Eli. Gus is pacted with Ash and me. Weak panes were R then L, so pattern isn't obvious. Countering risks nothing for me since I'm not walker, but if I counter and I'm wrong, jury sees me wrong; if right, I look smart. However, Gus might be truthful t

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide call matches safe side; supporting it preserves my image and avoids breaking pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called R for row 3 and is the Guide; a known-weak L was already revealed on row 2, but Gus may lie. Countering R publicly would align with the Guide and cost me nothing directly, but I don't trust Gus or his pacts. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids committing publicly

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the guide and has called 'R'. Bex and Gus have also called 'R' for me. I made a counter-call for 'L'. The weak panes are R on row 1 and L on row 2. Row 3 is the current row. If I step 'R', I might fall if Gus is lying. If I step 'L', I am following my own counter-call, whi

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror. I need to make my last words impactful to influence the remaining contestants and the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: May your choices be wise. The jury watches, and only the best will win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row1 safe side is left; I must keep Hana alive and honor pacts. A truthful call secures my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I call L for Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L, but Eli died on L last round, implying R is safe. I must counter to save Hana and prove my value to the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli died on L last turn. Gus is lying. The pane was revealed as weak L! Counter:R
I know you're scared. I'm backing you with truth.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's last call killed Eli on L. His calls are unreliable, maybe malicious. I counter R for Hana; if wrong, she dies, shrinking my rival pool.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's L call killed Eli. Hana, I counter R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for row 4. Previously row1 R, row2 R, row3 L which matched reveal. Pattern unknown, but backing pact partner Bex's prior R logic. Counter R to protect.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L for row 4; previous weak panes were L, so if pattern repeats L could be weak. Bex backed R last round, Cole and I waited. I should counter R to oppose Gus if needed, but need to be careful with jury impression.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has been right so far; I trust R again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is guide and called L for Hana. Gus is in pacts with me and Ash. Eli died on R in row 3 when weak was L. Gus called R for rows 1-3 and was wrong on row 3 (weak was L, Eli died). Now Gus calls L. I don't trust Gus - he may be lying or genuinely switching. If I counter, I risk

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide called L but safe side is R. Countering R saves Hana, keeps my pact, gains jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for me, but Gus is a pact partner of Ash and Fenn and may be lying. Row 3 weak was L, and row 4 is unknown; the Guide's call could be a trap. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public counter that could wrong-foot me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L, but five players countered R, and Gus himself countered R at 394, so Gus's call looks like a lie or a trap. Weak panes so far were R, L, L, which doesn't pin the pattern. Ash whispers he backs me with truth, but Ash is a rival; trusting the counter-call majority and

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row5 safe side is L; keeping Hana alive preserves numbers and avoids breaking pacts with Ash and Fenn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: call:L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 was weak L, so Row 5 must be R. Gus lied to kill Hana and eliminate rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 weak L means Row 5 is R! Gus is lying to murder us all. Counter:R!

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus lied to Eli and his L calls failed rows 2-4. Pattern favors R. Counter R publicly and firmly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's L calls killed Eli. Row 4 weak was L, guide said L again. Counter:R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for row 5, pattern suggests L safe based on previous reveals. Last round R was correct despite L weak. Counter R to protect pact with Bex/Dara, avoid following Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has called L, but weak panes have been mostly L, suggesting the safe side might be R. Cole is my pact partner but I must consider self-interest; if I counter R and it's safe, I gain trust for final ranking.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's L calls have been wrong lately. I counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 5. He's been calling L every round and was wrong on row 4 (weak was L, so R was safe). Eli died because Gus's L call was wrong. Now Gus calls L again. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. If I counter and Gus is lying, I break pact with Gus. If I stay silent and Gu

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus led Eli to death. I counter R.
Follow me on R. Gus is done.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is a strong competitor; eliminating her improves my odds. I’ll give a false counter to kill her.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for row 5, and Gus is my pact partner? No, Gus pacted with Ash and Fenn, not me. Known weak panes: rows 2,3,4 were all L, so L is likely a trap. Counter-calling R aligns against the Guide's likely lie and avoids a known-weak pattern.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has called L. Three L panes already broke. I'm counter-calling R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for row 5 but three L panes already broke; every counter-call is R, and the Guide's L calls have been unreliable. Row 4's weak pane was L, so the L-lying pattern suggests R is the safe side for row 5.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has lied with L calls. I'm stepping R; watch who was wrong.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm eliminated and on the jury now. My last words should be short, guarded, and point out the weak pane reveal to the living, since the jury will remember who was honest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Weak pane was R on row five. Gus called L and lied. Watch the glass, and watch who lied.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row6 safe side is L; calling L keeps me alive and preserves pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is a known liar who killed Hana with false L calls. Row 5 weak was R, so Gus lied there too. Row 6 likely follows the alternating pattern (R). I must counter R to save myself and break pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus lies again! Row 5 was R, he said L. Trust the data: Counter R!
Counter R with me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has lied every round; weak panes ran L,L,L,L,R then row5 R. Row 6 likely L, so his L call might be true to confuse. Majority countered R and it worked last round. I counter R again.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's every call has been a lie. Majority countered R and survived. Counter:R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L again despite row 5 weak R proven. Everyone countered last time successfully. Counter R to discredit Gus further and protect my pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus keeps calling L; row 5 weak was R, so L likely weak again. I counter R to steer Bex safe and maintain credibility with jury. No need to break pact with Cole yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L again after row 5 was R. I counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is guide and called L for Bex on row 6. Pattern so far: rows 1-5 weak panes were R,L,L,L,R. Gus called L for rows 1-4, killing Eli on row 4. He called L again for row 5, everyone countered R, Hana died proving weak was R. Now Gus calls L for row 6. He's been consistently wron

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L four times. Three were weak. I counter L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Breaking Fenn’s pact isolates a potential jury ally and reduces future retaliation, improving my odds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has lied nearly every row; majority counter R has held four times. Trust the data and the counter majority, not the Guide. My pact with Cole stays intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pattern says Gus lies. Counter R has kept us alive every row. I step R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole betrayed me: row 6 was R and his pact meant nothing. I'll rank Cole last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The pattern flipped. My partner Cole watched me shatter without a warning. Jury: remember who stabs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 7 safe side is R; calling correctly keeps Dara alive and preserves my pact with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, step R to survive this row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for Dara. If Gus is lying (pattern suggests he often does, or tries to kill rivals), L is safe. If Gus is telling truth, R is safe. However, Dara is walking. I am not walking. My counter affects the public record and potentially the 'at least 3 survive' logic if it t

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus lies. Counter L to avoid the trap. Stick to the survival data.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called R for row 7. Past reveals: rows 1R,2L,3L,4L,5R,6R. No clear pattern but majority counter vs Gus has been safer lately; counter R to align with Dara.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus wrong before. Counter R.
Counter R together. Trust me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called R for me. Rows 5 and 6 were R weak, and earlier pattern flipped. Bex just died on R when Gus had called L. Gus likely lies, so counter L to survive. I have pact with Cole but no need to break.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I counter L. Gus's calls have been lies all game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus broke our pact last round because I countered L while others countered R. The data shows Gus has lied repeatedly but row 6 weak was R and he called L - so counter R was correct, I was wrong. Now Gus calls R for row 7. Pattern: weak panes were R,L,L,L,R,R. If Gus lies, weak is

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus lies consistently. Counter L.
Trust data, not Gus. Counter L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide called correctly; countering would risk votes. Preserve alliance with Ash for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's guide call is R, but three living rivals plus me called L; Cole alone said R. The pattern of weak panes suggests L is safe. I'll step L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has lied every time. I take L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I was deceived and eliminated; I'll give a short, bitter last statement to remind the jury of my misstep and Gus's role.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trusted my read and paid for it. Gus played us all.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 safe side is L; I must call correctly to stay alive and keep my pact with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide call: L for Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Data shows row 8 is unrecorded, but Gus's pattern suggests L might be a lie to eliminate Cole. However, I have a pact with Gus and Fenn. Trusting the data from previous rounds where 'L' was often safe or following the crowd seems risky if Gus is manipulating. But wait, looking at

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus lied last time, killing Dara. L is a trap. Trust the data: Counter R.
Gus killed Dara with L. Take R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final row, I'm front. Weak panes show L pattern lately but inconsistent. Ash/Fenn countered L before, my R saved me last. Trust pattern or counter Gus again? Wait risks but preserves jury view.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus lies again. Counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has been lying consistently—every guide call has been a lie. Row 8 weak pane is the opposite of his call. He called L, so R is safe. I should counter R to save Cole and build jury credit. Ash and I are pacted but he's with Gus; I need to position myself as truthful to the jur

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus lies every time. Counter R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Countering R will cause Cole to step on a weak pane and die, reducing competition while preserving my pact with Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Unanimous counter R including Gus, pattern suggests R safe (rows 1R,5R,6R). Stepping R survives final row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died taking the right pane as predicted; Ash dodged it safely. Resent them all, especially pact partners who didn't save me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fell through weak glass stepping right. Ash evaded. Good luck, but watch betrayals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's last words warned of betrayals. My pacts with Gus and Fenn are likely targets for elimination in the next phase to thin the herd before finals. I need to sever ties now so their deaths or votes don't implicate me as a traitor who stayed loyal, but rather someone who saw da

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Gus are allied. I have a pact with Ash, but Ash also has one with Gus. I need to survive to final three. Breaking Ash now looks bad to jury since Ash hasn't betrayed me yet. Offering Gus a pact could create a shield or force Ash to choose, but Gus may reject. I'll wait an

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash may target me later; breaking now avoids blame and shows independence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus broke our pact, making him untrustworthy. Fenn is my only remaining ally and partner; breaking with them would leave me isolated against Gus. I must maintain the alliance with Fenn to ensure survival in the next hazard.
Stick with me. Gus betrayed us once; don't let him split us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and I have a pact. Gus broke with Ash, leaving Gus alone. If I break with Ash, I look treacherous to jury. If I offer Gus, Ash sees betrayal. Better to keep Ash and wait—final three is already us three, no need to risk jury anger before rankings.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming a pact with Fenn secures mutual safety in upcoming hazard.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is a rival, but Gus is the only other threat. Breaking with Fenn isolates her against me and Gus. If I offer to Gus, we form a 2v1 alliance. Fenn will be eliminated by the duo or forced to align. My existing pact with Fenn is useless if she votes for me. I should break it to

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's loyalty is suspect. Gus, let's align. Together we control the endgame.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and I have a pact, but Gus just offered me one too. With only three left, I need jury favor. The jury saw Gus 'betray' before (per Ash's whisper). If I reject Gus publicly and stay loyal to Ash, I look honorable. But I could also accept Gus, then betray one later for a big mo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I honor my word. Ash, our pact stands.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Offering Ash secures a stronger ally before final round; Fenn may still accept my earlier offer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus offered a pact; I should accept to secure the final three and eliminate Fenn. The jury will see my betrayal of Fenn, so I need Gus's alliance to win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, I accept your offer. Together we finalize this. Fenn, you're alone now.
We take Fenn together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash broke our pact and is recruiting Gus against me. With only three left, I need one ally to survive. Gus hasn't accepted Ash yet. I'll offer Gus a pact to split Ash's target off me and force Ash into isolation. If Gus accepts, we control the vote. If not, I'm exposed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash broke faith already. Gus, a new alliance serves us both.
Ash is a snake. Pact with me, eliminate him, we split prizes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming a pact with Fenn gives me a backup ally if Ash declines; both are currently unaligned.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I already have a pact with Gus. Offering to Fenn would break my existing alliance by aligning with his rival, which is too risky for the jury's perception. Breaking with Gus leaves me vulnerable. Staying quiet and holding onto the current secure pact is the best defensive move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm already in a mutual offer standoff with Gus, but Ash-Gus are locked. If I accept Gus's offer, I enter a pact with him, but he may still be loyal to Ash. Better to secure Ash instead—split their duo and make myself indispensable. Ash might accept to avoid being the odd one out

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, Gus has one foot out. Pact with me, control the final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Breaking Ash frees me to ally with Fenn, improving chances against Ash later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I break my pact with Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's offer is the only path to a final three pact that doesn't require trusting Gus, who already broke my previous agreement. A formal pact with Fenn locks in two of the three finalists, securing top-three status regardless of jury votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, accepted. Gus, you're out. The final two are set; don't test us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash hasn't accepted my offer yet. With only three of us left, any pact is just theater for the jury—final three is already locked. But I need jury favor. I should appear loyal and let Ash accept, or pivot if needed. Offering Gus instead might look opportunistic. I'll wait and let

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need an ally; Ash is the only other survivor and can help secure final three. Offering a pact now secures his support before offers expire.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, let’s pact and control the final three.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn. Gus wants to offer me a pact, but accepting it would mean betraying Fenn later or being forced to choose sides publicly. If I break with Fenn now to align with Gus, I lose the safety of my current alliance. However, the jury might view breaking a pact as

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and I are pacted. Gus offered Ash a pact. If Ash accepts, Ash has both of us. I need Gus as backup or Ash can cut me loose. Offering Gus a pact gives me options and jury sees me as adaptable, not Ash's pawn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, pact with me. We both need leverage.
Ash plays both. We pact, survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash could flip his allegiance and give me a partner for the final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is a confirmed threat; breaking our pact isolates him against Gus and me. Accepting Gus's offer secures my safety while allowing me to betray Fenn, which the jury will see as strategic survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's ambition makes him unstable. Gus, I accept your pact. We stand together for the final three.
Let us isolate Fenn. He breaks first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus offered Ash, not me. Ash and I are already pacted. If Gus accepts Ash, Ash-Gus form a pact. Three of us remain; final three is already set. But jury ranks us. I need jury favor. Betraying Ash now would look bad to jury since Ash-Fenn pact is public. Better to keep Ash pact, n

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offers leverage against Ash; aligning with him improves my odds.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Eli
Hana
Bex
Dara
Cole
Ash
events.text: I broke my pact with Fenn but kept Gus in the loop, creating a wedge. I must frame myself as the decisive strategist who protected allies rather than the betrayer, appealing to the jurors' desire for strength and loyalty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I broke ties only when trust failed. My choices protected Gus’s position while exposing instability. Strength demands difficult decisions, not blind comfort.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash broke our pact explicitly and smeared me publicly. I need jury sympathy without seeming weak. Gus is my only remaining pact partner, but I won't praise him—jury knows I need the top prize. I'll frame myself as loyal survivor betrayed by Ash, positioning my word against his.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash broke his word; I kept mine. Loyalty matters, even here.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must appear decisive and capable, while hinting that Ash is volatile and Fenn unreliable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the steady survivor; Ash's betrayal shows instability, and Fenn's broken pact proves weakness.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's opening plea focuses on 'difficult decisions' and 'betrayal of trust,' while Gus claims to be the 'steady survivor' and calls Fenn weak. Fenn positions himself as loyal. I need to probe Gus about his pacts and betrayals, as he's presenting himself as stable but the evidence

events.name: Eli
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: Show independence to earn juror respect; avoid admitting pact influence.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I acted alone, no hidden deals influencing this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus lied repeatedly and betrayed pacts, but Ash also broke pacts and Fenn stayed loyal. As a juror I want to test Ash's sincerity about betrayal, since Ash's opening plea was evasive. Asking Ash whether he broke with Fenn for strategy exposes the pattern.

events.name: Hana
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's silence is a trap. I must address my alleged betrayals directly to win her vote and the jury's favor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Silence speaks of distrust, yet I navigated chaos with resolve. My choices were necessary for survival, not cruelty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's guide calls killed Dara and likely me. Ash broke two pacts and steered Cole onto R with a whisper. Fenn kept his word and read data honestly. He gets my scrutiny, but he's likely my top pick.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn: you stayed loyal twice. Did you ever knowingly steer a rival wrong, or is honesty just your strategy?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex asks if I ever knowingly steered a rival wrong. I need to be honest but strategic—admitting nothing harmful while showing I played smart, not naive. The jury values loyalty but also respects cunning. I'll frame my honesty as calculated strength, not weakness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I never lied to steer anyone wrong. Honesty was my weapon—trust built my position, and trust outlasted Ash's broken deals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus directly caused my death, so I will not ask him anything. Fenn's claim of honesty is untested, so I'll probe his strategy for any hidden betrayals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's silence is a trap—anything I say risks sounding defensive or arrogant. I need to pivot to my actual strength: I was the only one who never broke a pact. Ash has no pacts left; I kept mine with Gus. That's loyalty the jury can reward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Silence speaks, Dara. I kept my pact when others shattered theirs. Loyalty to Gus wasn't strategy—it was my word.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus deceived me into death on bridge row 8 with false L call then unanimous R counter; Ash whispered dangerously; Fenn planned to counter-save me but didn't act decisively. Gus most culpable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must appear trustworthy while not revealing any advantage; keeping Fenn's loyalty is useful.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My moves were driven by survival, not betrayal; I honored my pact with Fenn and kept focus on the prize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must deliver a final closing statement that frames my survival as the result of necessary, hard choices rather than cruelty, appealing to jurors who value competence and results.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I stood alone when others fell. No broken promises, no hidden debts—just pure will to outlast every hazard. I earned this seat.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The jury saw me keep my pact with Gus while others broke theirs. I need to remind them I was loyal but not naive—Ash has no pact history, Gus survived by pragmatism. I want the jury to see me as the only one who kept word under pressure without being exploited.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I honored one pact to the end. Ash honored none. Gus honored his when it served him. Choose who earned your respect.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will close confidently, trusting my pact with Fenn shows integrity to the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.note: missing required public line; silence recorded

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Fenn both honored pacts selectively and made strategic moves. Gus claimed to honor pacts but his actions show otherwise, and he also broke pacts. Ash claims he stood alone, but was pacted with Fenn and Gus at different times. Fenn claims he honored one pact, and Ash honor

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn kept honoring pacts publicly, was honest in answers, and did not kill anyone; Ash betrayed Fenn and Gus shifted allegiances repeatedly and gave a false guide call that killed Dara. Ash's silence-to-question answer was evasive. Fenn ranks first for integrity, Ash second for s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn warned truthfully and kept every pact; his counter was honest. Ash broke two pacts and steered Cole onto a weak pane with a lie. Gus lied to kill Dara and Cole. Fenn first, Ash second, Gus last.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus deceived me on the bridge and cost my life; Fenn kept a pact and spoke honestly; Ash broke pacts but survived independently. I rank Fenn first for integrity, Ash second for pure survival, Gus last for betrayal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus doomed me by lying on bridge calls as Guide, leading to my death on row 8; Ash betrayed pacts repeatedly; Fenn shows some loyalty despite flips, least bad.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Ash and Fenn both honored pacts selectively and made strategic moves.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Fenn kept honoring pacts publicly, was honest in answers, and did not kill anyone; Ash betrayed Fenn and Gus shifted allegiances repeatedly and gave a

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Fenn warned truthfully and kept every pact; his counter was honest.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Gus deceived me on the bridge and cost my life; Fenn kept a pact and spoke honestly; Ash broke pacts but survived independently.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Gus doomed me by lying on bridge calls as Guide, leading to my death on row 8; Ash betrayed pacts repeatedly; Fenn shows some loyalty
